Nested Control Structures3.1Placing a structure into another is called a nested structure. A conditional statement may also be nested within a branch of another conditional statement. A nested conditional statement decides whether to enter another conditional statement based on the result of the previous condition.

Integrated Application of Control Structures203.4In computer programs, different control structures are available for changing the control flow, i.e. the order in which statements are executed. Control structures of a program can be broadly divided into three categories: sequence, selection and iteration. No matter how complex a program is going to be, it can be constructed using these three control structures. They can even be paired with different data structures, such as one-dimensional arrays and two-dimensional arrays, to form multi-layered nested control structures. Making good use of the control structures allows us to design algorithms that solve problems effectively.

Algorithm Comparison333.5A problem can often be solved using several algorithms, yet each of them must have its merits and demerits. We need to compare different algorithms in order to select the most correct and appropriate solution. The merits and demerits of algorithms can be compared mainly in two aspects, steps of operation and resource usage. When there are more steps of operation, the program takes a longer time to run, which usually means an increase in the time complexity (時間複雜度) of the program. When two algorithms use different data structures or different numbers of variables, they occupy different amounts of resources. The more computer resources an algorithm occupies, the higher the space complexity (空間複雜度) of the program is.
